[Thinking]
**Explaining multicolumn coloring**

I'm looking into how to span rows with multicolumn in LaTeX, and it seems to work. I can explain that \arrayrulecolor is used to color lines, while the colortbl package offers \rowcolor for coloring rows. 

In edge cases, if I’m using a colored row with \multicolumn, I should consider using \cellcolor, but \rowcolor should work regardless. 

I’ll create a minimal code snippet and provide a succinct explanation with examples!
[/Thinking]

\rowcolor is a LaTeX command (from the colortbl package, also available via xcolor with the table option) to color an entire table row.

How to enable:
- Prefer: \usepackage[table]{xcolor}
- Alternatively: \usepackage{colortbl}

Basic use:
\begin{tabular}{lcr}
\rowcolor{gray!20} % 20% gray background for this row
Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\
A & B & C \\
\rowcolor{yellow!30}
D & E & F \\
\end{tabular}

Notes and tips:
- Place \rowcolor just before the row you want to color.
- Works with color names (red, blue) and mixes like gray!20 or green!15!yellow!30.
- For alternating row colors, use:
  \rowcolors{2}{gray!10}{white}  % start at row 2
  ... your tabular ...
  \rowcolors{0}{}{}              % reset afterward
- Color a single cell: \cellcolor{<color>}
- Color a whole column: \columncolor{<color>}
- With booktabs, keep rules uncolored; you can still do:
  \arrayrulecolor{black} % default
  \toprule
  \rowcolor{gray!15} Header A & Header B \\
  \midrule
- If a colored row sits next to \hline/\toprule, put \rowcolor on the same line as the row’s content (not on a separate line).
- In longtables, load xcolor with table option before longtable and apply the same commands.

Minimal full example:
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[table]{xcolor}
\usepackage{booktabs}
\begin{document}
\begin{tabular}{lcr}
\toprule
\rowcolor{gray!20} Item & Qty & Price \\
Widget & 2 & \$10 \\
\rowcolor{yellow!25} Gizmo & 1 & \$15 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{document}
